q: How does a sponge iron plant in Barbil count power from its waste heat boiler?
title: Barbil sponge iron: waste heat power
short: Power from a waste heat recovery boiler on the kiln adds no new fuel, because the coal is already counted in the kiln. Do not add a grid factor for it. Count the kiln coal once, by mass balance, and treat waste heat power as your own zero-fuel supply that cuts grid purchases.
audience: Coal-based sponge iron plants in the Barbil and Keonjhar belt

ul: Coal fed to the kiln, with carbon content from lab tests.
Carbon left in sponge iron, char and dust.
Grid power bought on top, at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh.

p: Record generation from the turbine meter. It lowers Scope 2 by replacing grid units, but it is not a separate emission or a credit to subtract from Scope 1.
Direct reduced iron is a precursor for steel. Your steel buyer needs the kiln figure per tonne of sponge iron; electricity is not charged for iron and steel.
